text.p: Italy's BPT futures moved higher in early trading in line with other markets as investors took a more positive outlook on the market after two days this week of profit-taking and concerns over EMU delays, dealers said.

They added BTP were following the positive tone to bunds and T-bonds while worries over the single European currency starting on time were of secondary concern, but trading was generally cautious ahead of U.S. data due later this week.
"The profit-taking seems to have dried up, and we are now looking to push ahead following bunds," said one dealer on the LIFFE market.

Dealers said that concern emerging Tuesday from Germany over the EMU starting on time and Italy not being there at the start were largely dismissed in early trading. Markets were cautious ahead of U.S. GDP and jobs data on Thursday and Friday.
Generally steady dollar against the mark at just under 1.84 helped European bond markets, although there is still concern the Bundesbank may have to take some action to defend the mark.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said in a German newspaper interview today that the Bundesbank had to balance a weak economy against a weak mark.
